data: RealtimeJS uses an Adapter-Driven Architecture. This means the core engine contains the business logic, offline queueing, and state management, but it delegates the actual network operations to adapters.
data.creating-custom-adapters#Creating Custom:
You can build your own custom adapter for databases, storage, or transport. To ensure your custom adapter complies with the RealtimeJS standard, run it against our built-in Contract Test Suite!
import { runTransportAdapterContractTests } from '@realtimejs/core/src/adapters/ContractTestSuite';

data: RealtimeJS uses an Adapter-Driven Architecture. This means you can rip out our official adapters (like Socket.IO or Native WebSockets) and plug in your own proprietary transport layers without changing a single line of your React UI or business logic.

RealtimeJS is designed with the assumption that network connections are inherently unstable. Users will enter elevators, drive through tunnels, or simply experience ISP dropouts.The framework handles this transparently using an Offline Queueing architecture.
data.how-it-works#How It Works:
When a user attempts to send a message via client.chat.sendMessage() or the <MessageInput /> component, RealtimeJS checks the status of the TransportAdapter.
If Connected: The message is instantly forwarded to the server.
If Disconnected: The message is pushed into an in-memory offlineQueue.
Optimistic Render: In both cases, the React SDK instantly renders the message in the UI with a status of "sending".
data.automatic-reconnection#Automatic Reconne: You do not need to write any code to handle reconnections.When the TransportAdapter successfully reconnects to the server, it fires an internal event. The ChatModule intercepts this event, flushes the offlineQueue, and pushes all pending messages to the server in chronological order.

data: Optimistic UI is a frontend paradigm where the user interface updates instantly based on a user's action, assuming that the underlying network request will eventually succeed.RealtimeJS enforces an Optimistic UI architecture by default through its React SDK.
data.the-problem-with-traditional-uis#The Pro:
In a traditional application, sending a chat message looks like this:
User clicks "Send".
UI shows a loading spinner.
Network request travels to the server (100ms).
Server processes it and saves to database (50ms).
Network response travels back (100ms).
UI hides spinner and renders the message.
This results in a sluggish, 250ms+ delay for every single message.
data.the-realtimejs-approach#The RealtimeJS A:
When a user sends a message using @realtimejs/react, the following happens:
User clicks "Send".
The useSendMessage hook instantly generates a temporary UUID and injects the message into the local React state.
The UI renders the message instantly (0ms latency).
The hook asynchronously pushes the message through the ChatModule to the TransportAdapter.
When the server confirms receipt, the hook silently swaps the temporary UUID with the official database ID.
If the network request fails, the UI automatically flags the message with a red "Failed" status, allowing the user to retry.This creates an incredibly fluid, native-feeling user experience, identical to iMessage or WhatsApp.

data: Learn how to get RealtimeJS up and running in under 5 minutes.
data.installation#Installation:
RealtimeJS is built with modularity in mind. You need to install the core engine along with a transport adapter. If you are using React, you should also install the React SDK.
npm install @realtimejs/core @realtimejs/react @realtimejs/adapter-socketio socket.io-client

data: Welcome to RealtimeJS! 🚀RealtimeJS is a framework-agnostic realtime toolkit designed to help developers add realtime capabilities to applications with minimal setup and maximum flexibility. It provides a unified developer layer above various infrastructure providers like Socket.IO, WebRTC, and native WebSockets.
data.why-realtimejs#Why RealtimeJS?:
Today, developers often have to manually combine and configure raw WebSockets, Socket.IO, LiveKit, Redis, databases, and UI libraries to build even simple realtime applications. This results in:
High complexity
Slow development time
High maintenance costs
RealtimeJS solves this by providing a complete, plug-and-play toolkit with an adapter-driven architecture.
data.core-features#Core Features:
Adapter Driven: Swap between Socket.IO, Native WebSockets, or custom adapters without changing any core business logic.
Advanced Chat Mechanics: Built-in offline queueing, message status tracking, reactions, and editing.
Presence & Typing: Real-time user status tracking and typing indicators.
Optimistic UI: The official React SDK ensures user interactions feel zero-latency while syncing state in the background.
100% Type Safe: Written in strict TypeScript.
data.next-steps#Next Steps: Get started by installing the framework in the Getting Started guide!

data: The @realtimejs/react package provides a suite of highly optimized, production-ready React Hooks and context providers for building realtime interfaces instantly.It wraps the core engine with an Optimistic UI architecture, ensuring that user interactions feel zero-latency. It also heavily utilizes a Context-Driven Architecture, allowing you to bypass prop-drilling entirely by safely extracting state using useChatContext().
data.hooks-api#Hooks API:
useChatContext() - Safely extracts hoisted state inside a ChatProvider.
useUIConfig() - Exposes the features, ui, and updateConfig settings dispatcher.
usePresence() - Real-time user online/offline mapping.
useRealtime() - Access the raw core engine.
